long1.title: Sleep Prayer with Psalm 130 | Watching for the Morning (An Advent Bedtime Prayer, KJV)
long1.description:
A gentle Advent sleep prayer for anyone in a long season of waiting. We pray Psalm 130 slowly, one line at a time: crying out to God from the depths, setting down the day's regrets because "there is forgiveness with thee", resting our hope in His word, waiting for the Lord "more than they that watch for the morning", and trusting His plenteous mercy. We pray for others who are waiting tonight and close with a blessing. After the prayer, about 18 minutes of quiet music stays with you while you fall asleep.

Scripture (KJV): Psalm 130:1-7.

This prayer is not a substitute for professional care. If you are struggling, please reach out to someone you trust or a local helpline.

We will never ask you for money or to message us privately.

long2.title: Sleep Prayer for a Weary Heart | Rest from a Busy Season (with Gentle Rain, KJV)
long2.thumb_small: Sleep prayer for a weary heart
long2.description:
A calm guided sleep prayer, with the sound of gentle rain, for anyone worn out by a busy December. We come to Jesus with the whole heavy load (Matthew 11:28-29), let ourselves be comforted "as one whom his mother comforteth" (Isaiah 66:13), quiet the body from head to toe like David's "weaned child" (Psalm 131:2), rest in the God who "will rejoice over thee with joy" (Zephaniah 3:17), and fix our minds on Him for perfect peace (Isaiah 26:3). After the prayer, about 17 minutes of rain and quiet music stay with you while you fall asleep.

Scripture (KJV): Matthew 11:28-29; Isaiah 66:13; Psalm 131:2; Zephaniah 3:17; Isaiah 26:3.

This prayer is not a substitute for professional care. If you are struggling, please reach out to someone you trust or a local helpline.

long3.title: The Prince of Peace: Isaiah 9 Explained | Unto Us a Child Is Born (Advent Peace Sunday)
long3.description:
On the second Sunday of Advent, many churches light the candle of peace. In this video we go back to where the famous Christmas words "For unto us a child is born" were first spoken: to the lands of Zebulun and Naphtali around Galilee, the first region of Israel taken by the Assyrian army. We look at Isaiah's "Nevertheless", the people that walked in darkness seeing a great light, how Matthew shows that light coming first to Galilee when Jesus began His ministry, why the answer to the battle is a child, the four names Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace, and the peace Jesus gives "not as the world giveth". With a prayer for Peace Sunday.

Scripture (KJV): Isaiah 9:1-7; 2 Kings 15:29; Matthew 4:13-16; Luke 2:14; John 14:27.

This video is spiritual encouragement, not a substitute for professional care. If you are struggling, please reach out to someone you trust or a local helpline.
